After his wife's death, Dr. Andrew "Andy" Brown trades his career as a renowned neurosurgeon for an opportunity to be a better parent and move his two children to Everwood, Colorado.
Andy and Ephram's fragile relationship is further strained when it appears that Andy is again giving priority to his work. Meanwhile, Ephram's interest in Amy continues to develop.
Dr. Brown's clumsy attempt to come to Nina's defense for being a surrogate mother only makes the situation worse. Meanwhile, Amy cancels her party invitation to Ephram.
Drs. Brown and Abbott put aside their differences to educate the town of Everwood regarding a sexually transmitted disease. Meanwhile, Ephram ignores his feelings to comfort Amy.
Dr. Brown accompanies Ephram as he helps a deer return to the wilderness. Meanwhile, Ephram admits that he never asked his father to consider operating on Amy's comatose boyfriend.
Amy is heartbroken--and Ephram is furious--when Dr. Brown decides against performing a risky operation on Amy's comatose boyfriend. Delia is kept from playing with her only friend.
With the help of his friend and surgical partner from New York, Dr. Brown operates on Amy's comatose boyfriend, Colin. Amy relies on Ephram as she awaits the outcome.
As his wedding anniversary draws near, Dr. Brown questions whether he will ever feel like his life is worth living again. Meanwhile, Ephram and Amy share their first kiss.
Ephram and Delia's grandparents make an unexpected visit to check on their son-in-law--and they question Dr. Brown's parenting skills. Meanwhile, Ephram sneaks out to see Amy.
Delia and her grandmother, Nonny Ruth Hoffman, host a festive birthday party for a grumpy Edna. With everyone trapped due to a big snowstorm, Bright collapses from a burst appendix.
Ephram tries to recreate the Thanksgiving traditions of their mother as the Brown family spends its first holiday without her. Meanwhile, Dr. Brown must find a patient's brother.
When the owner of Everwood's flower shop dies, Dr. Brown discovers that she was growing marijuana in her backyard to help people who were suffering from cancer.
Dr. Brown begrudgingly auditions for a local production of "The King and I." Meanwhile, Ephram's feelings for Amy are complicated by Colin's desire to be his friend.
Ephram finds himself serving as confidante and friend to Colin, who continues to struggle to reclaim his life. Meanwhile, Dr. Brown hopes to convince Ephram to resume piano lessons.
